content: The technological offerings introduced by these global vendors are profoundly relevant to the specific operational challenges and strategic imperatives of the South African market. As local enterprises and governmental institutions rapidly migrate toward decentralized operational models and cloud-based architectures, the demand for sophisticated defensive mechanisms has surged. These sophisticated technological interventions are absolutely critical for mitigating the rapidly escalating risks associated with modern threat vectors. The accelerating role of artificial intelligence in facilitating complex cybercrime and deploying highly evasive ransomware has been identified as one of the most pressing security issues facing the global and regional digital landscape [11] . Global vendors bring unparalleled research and development resources, extensive global threat intelligence networks, and highly scalable AI models that effectively complement the localized innovations produced by South African firms. The confluence of major foreign investments, a highly dynamic local innovation ecosystem, and the urgent, continuous need to combat increasingly sophisticated, AI-enabled cyber threats ensures that South Africa will remain a pivotal growth market and a central pillar in the global cybersecurity defense architecture for the foreseeable future. In the absence of immediate access to these localized case studies, analysts often turn to global reports to contextualize the threat landscape, though these must be interpreted with caution. For example, analyses of global cyber threats provided by international organizations offer valuable insights into cybercrime trends and technological evolutions, but frequently focus on regions such as Asia and the South Pacific, thereby lacking South Africa-specific data [22] . The rapid digitalization of the South African economy has inadvertently expanded the attack surface for malicious actors, creating a fertile ground for sophisticated cyber threats. Historical data indicates a severe trajectory in this domain, evidenced by a 37 percent escalation in cyberattacks targeting South African government agencies in 2024 compared to the preceding year . A prominent example of this localized vulnerability was the significant disruption of the national weather service, a targeted event which underscored the increasing focus of cybercriminals on public sector entities and critical infrastructure [31] .
